decisions.evidence: Read the definition against the promised inventory: finite reduced crystallographic root system, Weyl group, positivity via a regular vector t, simple roots, root/coroot/weight groups, chambers and dominance. Existence of t, the lattice bases and the closed-chamber/stabilizer assertions are explicitly deferred to the following lemma rather than assumed, and rank-zero and empty conventions are stated. Sound as a definition; no proof obligation.

Checked 1.1-5.1. Regular vector by polynomial avoidance; strict Cauchy-Schwarz gives mn<4 and hence root sums, then nonpositive simple inner products; simple roots form a basis by cone and sign separation; each s_i permutes the other positive roots because only its own simple root flips; the coroot system is verified through the dual cone and reducedness; W preserves Q,Q^v,P and P is the dual lattice. Rank zero and choice-freeness checked.

Checked 1.1-4.1. The first positive-to-negative change is the own simple root, giving the deletion formula s_beta = u s_i u^{-1}; both descent inequalities are strict; n(w)=l(w) by induction on reduced words; the first nonreduced prefix yields a two-letter deletion after reversal. Nonreduced inputs and rank zero included; no Coxeter presentation or exchange axiom is used.

Checked 1.1-3.1: existence of a closed-chamber representative by maximizing (rho,x); uniqueness by minimal-length cancellation with the isometry identity; stabilizer generation by induction on length; chambers equal sign regions and simple transitivity; longest element w_0 with length |Phi^+| and w_0^2=1. Singular wall points, the zero weight and rank zero verified.

The definition's well-definedness proof was read: the saturated-reflection-chain relation is a partial order before any subword claim; the four-case lifting property rests on strong exchange; chain implies subword by descending deletion; subword implies chain by finite induction. Expression independence and rank zero are included, and no abstract Coxeter presentation is substituted.

Definition only. The group algebra of the weight lattice, its automorphism action and the distinct-element orbit sums m_lambda are correctly set up; m_0=1, stabilizers do not multiply coefficients, rank zero gives C, and no representative family is chosen. Sound.

Checked 1.1-2.1: invariance is coefficient constancy on orbits; orbit sums span and are independent; reindexing by dominant weights via the unique representative; the norm bound ||mu|| <= ||lambda|| bounds the integral coordinates so each dominant ideal is finite. Wall weights, the zero invariant and rank zero verified; choice-free.

Definition with justifications: coordinate-free symmetric algebra, pullback action by graded automorphisms, invariant algebra R, positive ideal I=SR_+, coinvariant quotient, Reynolds projection R-linearity and idempotence, polynomial-function faithfulness, and the V=0 and G=1 boundary cases. The claims are correctly derived; no proof obligation.

Checked 1.1-3.1: disjoint finite orbits, least-coordinate factors that are zero and one at the needed points, the product interpolation q and its Reynolds average. q is zero on O1 and one on O2, and invariance is preserved by averaging; singleton and zero orbits are covered and no AC is used.

The definition and its two derived claims were checked: pairwise nonproportional factors by reducedness and positivity; reflection hyperplanes equal root hyperplanes via the proper-subspace covering argument and the regular-point criterion; w.Delta = det(w)Delta by multiplying over simple-reflection words. Rank zero gives Delta=1.

Checked 1.1-2.1: each linear factor divides an anti-invariant by vanishing on its reflecting hyperplane plus coordinate constancy; pairwise nonproportional factors multiply using primeness; quotient invariance follows by cancellation with det(w) nonzero in the domain; uniqueness and the zero polynomial are covered.

Checked 1.1-4.1. Reynolds degree induction gives R=C[f_j] for any generating set; 1.2's relation lemma is proved by transforming with a generating reflection and averaging; the Euler/derivative argument forces f_j into the ideal of the others, contradicting irredundancy. Trivial group, V=0 and degree-one cases checked; the trivial-group averaging step remains valid because a positive-degree element lies in I=R_+ there.

Checked 1.1-6.1 against F3-F7: orbit monic equations give generation over R and common zero set {0}; growth counts force m=n; the local ring is CM by the coordinate parameter sequence; graded regularity descends to S; the Hilbert series yields a degreewise free basis. The published depth/CM/parameter statements were read and their hypotheses (nonzero finite module, Noetherian local ring) are satisfied here.

Checked 1.1-3.1: Hilbert series product from the regular sequence; Molien via diagonalizable finite-order operators and explicit eigenvalue bases; the limit t->1 isolates prod d_i = |W|, using faithfulness to exclude r unit eigenvalues for a nonidentity element. Rank zero gives W={1} and empty products 1.
